title: How to transport a refrigerator
meta_title: How to transport a refrigerator — CargoPT
meta_description: See how to prepare, protect and transport a refrigerator, including access, position and care after delivery.
hero_description: Transport requires preparation, adequate protection, tilt control and a route compatible with the dimensions of the refrigerator.
direct_answer_heading: Transport the refrigerator empty, protected and as vertical as possible
direct_answer: To transport a refrigerator, empty it, switch it off, defrost it and dry it completely. Remove or secure shelves, drawers, cables and other moving parts. Measure the appliance, doors, lifts, corridors and stairs before the job; protect its surfaces and plan the route to the vehicle. Keep the refrigerator as upright as possible while moving it and secure it so it cannot shift. If it was tilted significantly, check the model manual and follow the manufacturer's stated waiting time before switching it on again.
key_points: Measure the refrigerator and every point along the route; also send access photos.
Use helpers and means appropriate to the weight.
Keep the device as vertical as possible.
Attach it to the vehicle and follow the manual before starting it.

sections.heading: What to do before transport
paragraphs: The refrigerator must be empty, switched off, defrosted and dry. Shelves, drawers, cables and pipes need to be removed or immobilized.
Also check if there is water accumulated in the tray, dispenser or connections. Incomplete preparation may cause spills during movement.

sections.heading: Measure equipment and route
paragraphs: Record height, width and depth, including handles and other protruding elements. Measure doors, elevators, hallways, landings and stair turns.

Confirm where the vehicle can stop and the distance to the entrance. If the refrigerator does not fit at any point, it may be necessary to dismantle the property's doors or components authorized by the manufacturer.
checklist: Width of doors in both properties.

sections.heading: How to move a refrigerator
paragraphs: A refrigerator is bulky, heavy and difficult to hold. It must not be dragged directly over the floor or moved only by doors or handles.
Use a suitable cart, straps and protection. The number of helpers must correspond to the weight, dimensions and access.

items.title: Protected floor
items.text: Use adequate protection to avoid risks and damage during exit and entry.

items.title: Transport cart
items.text: Choose equipment compatible with the weight and secure the refrigerator before moving it.

items.title: Straps
items.text: They must stabilize the device without crushing doors, panels or pipes.

items.title: Helpers
items.text: Stairs, gaps and large models may require a reinforced team.

sections.heading: In what position should it travel
paragraphs: The refrigerator must be transported as vertically as possible. The slope must be limited to what is necessary to overcome access points and use handling equipment.
When transport in a different position is unavoidable, consult the manual or manufacturer first. Allowed orientation and waiting time before connection vary between models.

sections.heading: How to protect the refrigerator in the vehicle
paragraphs: Place the equipment in a stable area, protected by blankets and without direct contact with hard or sharp items.
Attach it to suitable points on the vehicle to prevent movement, falls and impacts during braking and cornering. Do not place heavy items on the refrigerator.

sections.heading: What to do after delivery
paragraphs: Place the refrigerator in its final location, check that it is stable and confirm that cables and tubes have not been trapped or damaged.
Do not automatically turn it on right after arrival if it has been tilted. Consult the manufacturer's instructions and respect the period indicated for the model.

sections.heading: How to prepare a comparable request
paragraphs: To help carriers assess the same job, provide the route, refrigerator model and dimensions, photos, floors, lifts, stairs, parking distance and whether you need helpers, packing or installation.

In an anonymised internal review of 77 requests submitted through the CargoPT form from 28 June to 2 September 2026, 102 pickup or delivery addresses were above ground level and 27 were marked as having no lift. The sample covers several transport types: it illustrates why access details matter, but does not predict price or guarantee offers.
checklist: Addresses and preferred date or time window.
Photos of the appliance and access points.
Floors, lifts, stairs and parking distance.

mid_cta.heading: Plan the transport of the refrigerator
mid_cta.text: Send dimensions, photos, route and access. If suitable carriers are available, you can compare any offers received.

faq.question: Can the refrigerator be transported lying down?
faq.answer: It is recommended to keep it as vertical as possible. If another position is unavoidable, confirm in advance in the manual or with the manufacturer which orientation is permitted.

faq.question: Can I turn on the refrigerator immediately?
faq.answer: It depends on the position and model. If there was a tilt, follow the waiting period indicated by the manufacturer before turning on.

faq.question: How many people are needed?
faq.answer: It depends on the weight, dimensions and access. Large models, stairs and lack of elevator may require more helpers.

faq.question: Is it necessary to remove the refrigerator doors?
faq.answer: Only when access requires it and the procedure is permitted by the manufacturer. It must be done by someone with adequate knowledge.

faq.question: What information should I include in the order?
faq.answer: Indicate dimensions, type of refrigerator, floors, elevators, stairs, parking, route and photographs of access.
